pr.title: Build the installer with Inno Setup 6.7.3 and drop pre-Windows 10 leftovers
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 0a of the modernization roadmap. The installer has required Windows 10 since the libpq 18 upgrade, so the parts it still carried for older Windows can go. So can the Inno Setup 6.2.2 pin, which only existed for Vista.

| Change | Details |
|---|---|
| **Inno Setup 6.2.2 → 6.7.3** (latest) | Installed in CI from the official GitHub release and checked against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes. Chocolatey only has 6.7.1. ISCC is located from the installation, not a fixed path. |
| Inno 6.3/6.4 deprecations | `x64` → `x64compatible`, `FileCopy` → `CopyFile` |
| One Visual C++ runtime | Ships the newest installed runtime only. The 14.29 tier for Vista through 8.1 is gone. |
| Universal CRT | No longer shipped (Windows 10+ has it built in). The 44 checked-in `Microsoft.UCRT.WindowsSDK14393` DLLs and `Test-DownlevelForwarders.ps1` are removed. **Upgrades delete the stale copies from Bin.** |
| Dead code | `isxdl.dll` and `[Run]` entries for MSI 2.0, IE6, MDAC, JET and .NET 2.0. They read a `dep.ini` that nothing writes. |
| Small cleanups | Pre-Windows 7 branch in `GrantServiceAccountAccess`; unused `Install-ChocoPackage.ps1` |

Not changed yet: the C++ toolset (v142) and the ATL setup in CI. Those move in Phase 0b, together with C++20 and the hardening flags.

## Tests

New `Infrastructure\InstallationLayout` regression tests check that the installed Bin folder:
- has the Visual C++ runtime,
- has a runtime not older than the 14.29 toolset,
- contains no Universal CRT files.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

-function Test-DownlevelForwarders {
-    # Fails if any DLL in $Path exports a forwarder whose module part carries its own ".dll"
-    # extension - "module.dll.Function" rather than "module.Function".
-    #
-    # The loader in Windows Vista cannot resolve that form. Windows 10 can, so a build made
-    # with a newer Universal CRT redistributable passes every test on a modern machine and
-    # then dies at startup on Vista with an access violation in ntdll, before any hMailServer
-    # code runs. That is what happened when the build moved to GitHub Actions and the
-    # Universal CRT went from the 10.0.10240 redistributable to the SDK's 10.0.19041: 27 of
-    # its forwarders use the new form, three of them ones ucrtbase.dll itself imports.
-    #
-    # Imports are not enough to catch this - both sets import the same functions from the same
-    # modules. Only the forwarder strings differ, which is why this checks them directly.
-    #
-    # Passing is necessary, not sufficient. Microsoft supports no Universal CRT newer than
-    # 10.0.14393 on Windows Vista through 8.1 - see "Universal CRT deployment" on Microsoft
-    # Learn - and a redistributable above that ceiling can fail there in ways this does not
-    # look for. Keep to a supported version; this only catches the one that got through.
-    param(
-        [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Path
-    )
-
-    $dumpbin = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles} 'Microsoft Visual Studio\*\*\VC\Tools\MSVC\*\bin\Hostx64\x64\dumpbin.exe') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
-        Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
-    if (-not $dumpbin) { throw "dumpbin.exe was not found; it ships with the Visual C++ build tools." }
-
-    $offenders = @()
-    foreach ($file in Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $Path '*.dll')) {
-        foreach ($line in (& $dumpbin.FullName /exports $file.FullName)) {
-            if ($line -match '\s(\S+)\s+\(forwarded to\s+([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+\.dll)\.(\S+)\)') {
-                $offenders += "$($file.Name): $($Matches[1]) -> $($Matches[2]).$($Matches[3])"
-            }
-        }
-    }
-
-    if ($offenders) {
-        throw "These forwarders cannot be resolved by the Windows Vista loader, which the installer still supports (MinVersion in section_setup.iss):`n" +
-              ($offenders -join "`n") +
-              "`nShip a redistributable that writes them as <module>.<function>, or drop Vista support."
-    }
-
-    "No forwarders that the Windows Vista loader cannot resolve were found in $Path."
-}

+[InstallDelete]

+; than 10. Windows 10 and later carry the Universal CRT themselves and never load these
+; copies, so an upgrade removes them rather than leaving them behind in Bin.

+Type: files; Name: "{app}\Bin\ucrtbase.dll"

commit.message:
Build the installer with Inno Setup 6.7.3 and drop pre-Windows 10 leftovers

The installer requires Windows 10 since libpq 18, so what it still carried for older
Windows can go, and so can the Inno Setup 6.2.2 pin that only existed for Vista.

- Inno Setup 6.7.3 (latest), installed in CI from its GitHub release and checked
  against the SHA-256 GitHub publishes, since Chocolatey only has 6.7.1. ISCC is
  located from the installation rather than a fixed path.
- x64 becomes x64compatible (deprecated in 6.3), FileCopy becomes CopyFile (6.4).
- Ship only the newest Visual C++ runtime. The 14.29 "legacy" tier, the checked-in
  Universal CRT (Microsoft.UCRT.WindowsSDK14393) and Test-DownlevelForwarders.ps1
  existed only for Windows Vista through 8.1. An upgrade deletes the old UCRT files
  from Bin, which Windows 10 never loads.
- Remove the isxdl.dll downloader and the [Run] entries that installed MSI 2.0,
  IE6, MDAC, JET and .NET 2.0 from a dep.ini nothing writes - all dead code.
- Remove the pre-Windows 7 branch in GrantServiceAccountAccess and the unused
  Install-ChocoPackage.ps1.

New regression tests (Infrastructure\InstallationLayout) check that Bin has the
Visual C++ runtime, not older than the 14.29 toolset, and no Universal CRT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
